$comment: Theory registry SEED. Records verified by deep-research pass 1 (2026-06-20, 3-vote adversarial, all 3-0 primary-source). Schema: ./registry-schema.md. Pass-2 constructs (Kirton, Rhodes, Guilford, Csikszentmihalyi, Sawyer, Kaufman-Beghetto, ...) are intentionally absent until verified. Never add an unverified record.

records.primary_work: A Propulsion Model of Types of Creative Contributions, Review of General Psychology 3(2):83-100
records.core_claim: Creative contributions differ not only in the amounts of creativity they display but also in the types — classified by stance toward a field's prevailing paradigm (4 types accept current paradigms, 3 reject them).

lineage.note: 1999 defines 7 types; later expanded to 8 (added integrate/reinitiate). Anchor to 1999.

records.history_note: A deliberate turn away from amount-of-creativity scoring (Guilford/Torrance lineage) toward a typology of KINDS of contribution by paradigm stance — the canonical 'style, not score' move on the contribution side.
caveats: Anchor the record to the 1999 7-type version; treat the 8-type expansion as a lineage edge, not the origin.

records.primary_work: The Creative Mind: Myths and Mechanisms (rev. 2004); concise statement in 'Creativity in a Nutshell'
records.core_claim: Creativity is the ability to come up with ideas or artefacts that are new, surprising, and valuable, via three routes: combinational (unfamiliar combinations of familiar ideas), exploratory (new ideas within a conceptual space), and transformational (changing the space itself).

lineage.note: Both are type-of-creativity typologies; Boden's is computational and space-relative.

records.history_note: The canonical COMPUTATIONAL creativity typology, built to be intelligible to AI. 'Conceptual spaces are structured styles of thought... not originated by one individual mind' — creativity is relative to an inherited space, which is why transformational creativity (changing the space) is the rarest and most surprising.
caveats: ResearchGate PDF intermittently 403s; use SEP or interaliamag.org reprint as stable mirrors.
Boden's triad describes the CREATIVE ACT (process) and its outputs; mapping it to coding-move types is analogical, not validated.

records.primary_work: The Social Psychology of Creativity (1983); canonical restatement: 'Componential Theory of Creativity', HBS Working Paper 12-096 (2012)
records.core_claim: Any creative response requires four components: three within the person (domain-relevant skills, creativity-relevant processes, intrinsic task motivation) and one outside it (the social/work environment). Creativity = outcomes both novel and appropriate on a heuristic task.

lineage.note: Both place an environmental/social locus alongside the individual (Amabile's 'environment' ~ Rhodes' Press).

records.history_note: Brought social psychology into a field dominated by personality/cognition. The 'intrinsic motivation principle' is its signature and its most contested tenet; Amabile's later 'motivational synergy' work qualified it.
caveats: 'creativity-relevant processes' was 'creativity-relevant SKILLS' in the 1983 version.
Do NOT claim extrinsic motivators are always harmful — motivational synergy shows some help.
Uniquely names a Press (environment) component — useful for framing a coding session as person-in-environment-with-agent.

records.scholar: Nicole Forsgren, Jez Humble, Gene Kim
records.primary_work: Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution, 2018); academic grounding: 'A Taxonomy of Software Delivery Performance Profiles', AMCIS 2020
records.core_claim: Four key software-delivery-performance metrics: deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, time to restore service (two throughput, two stability).

lineage.note: Shared lead author (Forsgren); SPACE generalizes beyond delivery to multidimensional productivity.

records.history_note: Moved DevOps from anecdote to measurement via large-N survey + cluster analysis (n=7,522). The four metrics are durable; the famous Elite/High/Medium/Low LADDER is a later annual-report artifact, not in the book and not peer-reviewed.
caveats: REFUTED (0-3): the 4-tier Elite/High/Medium/Low scheme is NOT from the 2018 book and NOT peer-reviewed; the AMCIS paper found THREE empirical clusters. Treat 4-tier as popular reporting.

SESSION-OBSERVABILITY: deployment frequency, change failure rate, time-to-restore generally need production/incident data and are NOT observable from one coding session. Only lead-time-like intervals and activity/flow are session-observable.

records.scholar: Forsgren, Storey, Maddila, Zimmermann, Houck, Butler
records.primary_work: The SPACE of Developer Productivity: There's more to it than you think, ACM Queue 19(1):20-48, DOI 10.1145/3454122.3454124
records.core_claim: Developer productivity is multidimensional and cannot be captured by a single metric or dimension. Five dimensions: Satisfaction, Performance, Activity, Communication/collaboration, Efficiency/flow (use at least three).

lineage.target_id_or_name: single-metric productivity measurement (incl. naive use of DORA)
lineage.note: Explicitly argues against reducing productivity to one number.

records.history_note: The strongest delivery-side warrant for 'style, not score': a peer-reviewed source from the DORA authors themselves cautioning against single-metric evaluation of developers.
caveats: 'Tom' vs 'Thomas' Zimmermann are the same author.
Also reprinted in Communications of the ACM 64(6):46-53 (2021).

records.primary_work: The Uses of Argument (Cambridge University Press)
records.core_claim: An argument decomposes into claim, data/grounds, warrant, backing, qualifier, rebuttal. The warrant is the bridge justifying the leap from data to claim; backing is the evidence supporting the warrant.

lineage.note: Kane applies Toulmin's structure to assessment validity, recommending the full argument be made explicit for high-stakes decisions.

records.history_note: Toulmin's layout of argument is the schema's spine: 'backing' is the citation hook, and chained inferences (one claim becomes the next's datum) give the genealogy hook for a whole lineage of reasoning.

records.scholar: Lee J. Cronbach, Paul E. Meehl
records.primary_work: Construct Validity in Psychological Tests, Psychological Bulletin 52(4):281-302
records.core_claim: Construct validation applies when an attribute is not operationally defined; a construct is admissible only if embedded in a nomological net whose laws touch observables; the interpretation must be falsifiable — 'Rationalization is not construct validation.'

lineage.target_id_or_name: Messick unified construct validity; Borsboom (2009); Haig
lineage.note: The 1955 four-type validity taxonomy was later collapsed/unified and critiqued; cite 1955 for the origin record.

records.history_note: The discipline that prevents citation theater. Supplies the warrant-strength tiers: validated operationalization (net contact with observables) > analogical proxy > metaphorical inspiration.
caveats: Nomological-net theory has been critiqued/superseded as a forward-looking theory of validity, but remains accurately attributable as the 1955 origin.

records.primary_work: An Analysis of Creativity, Phi Delta Kappan 42(7):305-310
records.core_claim: Creativity analyzes into four interdependent strands — Person, Process, Press, Product — distinct analytical lenses, not a typology of people. Verbatim: 'the four P's of creativity, i.e., (1) person, (2) process, (3) press, (4) products.'
records.history_note: Grounds the registry's own `measures` field. The four Ps are loci of analysis, interdependent in function ('only in unity do the four strands operate functionally'). OpenStory observes the PROCESS strand — which is exactly why Person/Product constructs cap at analogical.
caveats: Primary PDF is FlateDecode-compressed and could not be machine-parsed; rests on consistent secondary reproductions of the verbatim text.
Journal is Phi Delta Kappan (some snippets misspell 'Phi Beta Kappan').

records.primary_work: Adaptors and Innovators: A Description and Measure, Journal of Applied Psychology 61(5):622-629
records.core_claim: The KAI rates respondents on a continuous adaptor↔innovator dimension of cognitive STYLE, explicitly independent of cognitive LEVEL/capacity ('no better style'; correlations with ability tests < 0.1).

lineage.note: Separates creative STYLE from the divergent-thinking ABILITY/level tradition Guilford launched.

records.history_note: The cleanest 'style not level' instrument and the natural anchor for an adaptor↔innovator archetype axis. PERSON-locus, so linking it to OpenStory's process signal is analogical, never validated.
caveats: 'measures cognitive style to the exclusion of cognitive level' is a paraphrase (Wikipedia/kai.foundation), NOT Kirton's 1976 verbatim — do not present as a 1976 quotation.
kai.foundation is vendor-adjacent; substance corroborated by the peer-reviewed article + secondary literature.
Taylor (1989) challenges the three-factor sufficiency — cite as a starting point, not pure confirmation.

records.core_claim: The agenda-setting address that put creativity on psychology's agenda ('The neglect of this subject by psychologists is appalling'); introduces the divergent vs convergent production distinction within the Structure of Intellect program.

lineage.note: The ability/level measurement tradition that operationalized divergent thinking (TTCT unverified — pending pass).

records.history_note: The modern origin point for creativity research. Divergent/convergent is the proto-style distinction Kirton later reframed as style-not-level. Person/ability locus.
caveats: Best cited as the agenda-setting / call-to-arms text; the full divergent/convergent apparatus is the broader Structure of Intellect program.
A weak hosting domain surfaced the PDF; bibliographic facts rest on Oxford Bibliographies, Taylor & Francis, SciRP.

records.primary_work: Creativity: Flow and the Psychology of Discovery and Invention (HarperCollins)
records.core_claim: Flow — a state of optimal experience marked by intense concentration and deep enjoyment during an activity; a transient in-activity experiential state.

lineage.note: Same author/book; a separate construct at a different locus.

records.history_note: PROCESS-locus → one of only three constructs in the registry eligible for a VALIDATED (not merely analogical) warrant against session-event signals (e.g. sustained, uninterrupted tool cadence).
caveats: Challenge-skill balance is a precondition of flow, not flow itself.
Do not conflate with the systems model (different locus).

records.primary_work: Society, Culture, and Person: A Systems View of Creativity (in The Nature of Creativity, ed. Sternberg)
records.core_claim: Creativity emerges from the interaction of person × domain × field, not the individual alone.

lineage.note: Both add an environmental/social locus alongside the individual.

records.history_note: The systems/Press model — creativity as a property of a system, not a person. Aligns with OpenStory framing a session as person + agent + domain.
caveats: ATTRIBUTION ONLY: the 1988/1999 systems-model chapters were NOT separately fetched in pass 2; rests on the documented contents of the 1996 book. Lower evidentiary footing than the Flow claim — re-verify before citing as backing.

records.primary_work: Distributed Creativity: How Collective Creations Emerge From Collaboration, Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts 3(2):81-92
records.core_claim: Collaborative emergence / 'distributed creativity': a nonindividualistic group process whose creative product is determined by no single participant. Four marks: unpredictable outcome, moment-to-moment contingency, interactional contingency, roughly equal contribution.

lineage.note: Extends the social/distributed view of creativity to moment-to-moment group interaction.

records.history_note: PROCESS (collaborative) locus. ⚠️ REFUTES the 'Conductor' archetype: Sawyer places the conductor-led orchestra at the PREDICTABLE/CONSTRAINED pole as his counter-example — the OPPOSITE of emergence. Verbatim: 'a symphony orchestra performs from a score and is guided by a conductor' is the predictable example; single-individual-controlled encounters are LESS likely to manifest collaborative emergence.
caveats: A leadership/orchestration archetype CANNOT be grounded here — it would invert the author's meaning.
Empirical basis: interaction analysis of 5 improvised teen-theater performances (ages 11-17).

records.scholar: James C. Kaufman & Ronald A. Beghetto
records.primary_work: Beyond Big and Little: The Four C Model of Creativity, Review of General Psychology 13(1):1-12
records.core_claim: Four-C: mini-c (creativity in learning), little-c (everyday), Pro-c (professional-level expertise), Big-C (eminent). A developmental trajectory of magnitude, not a style typology.

lineage.note: Extends a two-level scheme into a four-level developmental trajectory.

records.history_note: DEGREE, not style → feeds a growth-edge / trajectory axis, never the style axis. One can be Pro-c in one domain and little-c in another (not a fixed tier).
caveats: mini-c is intrapersonal/subjective (novel 'to the person'), leaning Process — so not a pure magnitude band.

records.primary_work: The cognitive neuroscience of creativity, Psychonomic Bulletin & Review 11(6):1011-1026
records.core_claim: Four basic types of creative INSIGHT from crossing two processing modes (deliberate vs spontaneous) × two content sources (cognitive vs emotional), each mediated by a distinct neural circuit.

lineage.note: Both are process-level typologies of the creative act rather than of creators.

records.history_note: ⭐ PROCESS-locus + a style-like 2×2 typology → the strongest candidate for a VALIDATED (not merely analogical) style axis matched to session-event signals (deliberate/sequenced vs spontaneous/exploratory work). A possible process-native alternative to a Person-locus style axis.
caveats: It taxonomizes INSIGHTS, not creators; popularized blogs misread it as 'four types of creative people' — do not.

records.scholar: Colin G. DeYoung, Quilty, Peterson & Gray
records.primary_work: Openness to Experience, Intellect, and Cognitive Ability, Journal of Personality Assessment 96(1):46-52
records.core_claim: Within Big Five Openness/Intellect, Openness and Intellect are separable aspects (measured by the BFAS): Intellect tracks general intelligence; Openness tracks verbal/aesthetic engagement.

lineage.note: A mid-level 'aspect' split below the domain (DeYoung, Quilty & Peterson 2007).

records.history_note: PERSON-locus trait aspects → analogical only. Useful for interpretation, not a style axis.
caveats: Single two-sample study (N=125 / N=189), not meta-analytic; 'Intellect tracks g' lightly simplifies 'independently associated with g'.
